reflection: Volume-contrast factors (AAPL vs QQQ/NVDA volume z-scores) are the only family that clears bars; they help 2023 and 2025 and fail in 2022 and 2024. Scaling by Apple's range or volatility reduced the 2024 loss, and the range-scaled NVDA version joined the team. The best pair was the 60d-vol-scaled ratio with qqq_volume_vs_price_divergence (4/4 years). Price-only and gap-type factors keep failing, so I will stay in the volume family, use range/vol scaling, and test QQQ-volume-divergence variants and a partner for the range-scaled team factor.

lessons.name: aapl_vs_qqq_volume_60d_vol_scaled_ratio
lessons.lesson: Dividing by 60d Apple volatility kept the 2023/2025 gains and helped the team 3/4 years, and it complements QQQ volume divergence, but 2022 and 2024 alone still lose.

lessons.name: aapl_vs_nvda_volume_surge_range_scaled
lessons.lesson: Scaling the volume contrast by today's range is better than by past volatility because it adapts to the current day's turbulence and helped both models, though 2024 still lost.

lessons.name: aapl_drawdown_from_60d_high_vs_qqq
lessons.lesson: Relative drawdown is a price-level trend measure that overlaps existing momentum factors and flipped sign in 2024.

lessons.name: aapl_gap_fill_persistence
lessons.lesson: Gap times intraday direction is noisy and only worked in 2025, so overnight/intraday gap structure carries little next-day information.

lessons.name: qqq_range_compression_60d
lessons.lesson: QQQ range compression is a slow volatility regime proxy that lost in 2022 and 2024 and added nothing even in pairs.

lessons.name: msft_nvda_return_vs_aapl_volume_confirm
lessons.lesson: Multiplying a peer-vs-QQQ return gap by QQQ volume produced a noisy product that hurt in nearly every year.

factors.name: aapl_vs_qqq_volume_range_scaled
factors.hypothesis: The 60d-vol-scaled ratio lost in 2022 and 2024 probably because slow volatility doesn't reflect today's conditions; the range scaling that worked for the NVDA version should adapt the QQQ contrast to the current day.

factors.name: qqq_volume_vs_move_divergence_60d
factors.hypothesis: The divergence using absolute close return lost in 2024; using intraday range and a 60d baseline gives a steadier measure of volume not explained by price movement and may be less regime-dependent.

factors.name: aapl_dollar_volume_vs_qqq_dollar_volume
factors.hypothesis: Dollar-volume participation compares Apple's capital flow with the market's, adjusting for price level drift that share volume ignores.

factors.name: aapl_range_vs_volume_efficiency
factors.hypothesis: Range that is large relative to volume (or small with heavy volume) signals absorption or thin trading, which may predict reversal in the next day.

factors.name: aapl_nvda_volume_range_scaled_x_qqq_div
factors.hypothesis: The team's range-scaled Apple volume factor paired well with QQQ volume divergence in earlier tests; scaling the market divergence by QQQ range makes a market-state partner on the same scale.

factors.name: msft_volume_vs_aapl_volume_range_scaled
factors.hypothesis: Adds a MSFT-based peer volume contrast to the market divergence factor; MSFT is the peer whose return is most useful, and range scaling worked for the NVDA variant.
